newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo Nikkei ends below 20,000, hurt by Tokai news.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo Nikkei ends below 20,000, hurt by Tokai news.

text.p: The Tokyo stock market's benchmark Nikkei index ended below the 20,000 level on Friday, the first time it has done so since the end of May, depressed by news in the afternoon that construction firm Tokai Kogyo Co Ltd had decided to apply for court protection, brokers said.
The Nikkei average finished 153.41 points or 0.76 percent lower at 19,968.00. It last closed below 20,000 on May 27 at 19,889.89. During the session, it fell as low as 19,907.39.
Nikkei 225 September futures ended 260 points down at 19,910.

"The Tokai news depressed stocks but the impact was somewhat limited as there had been rumours about the company in the past and the market had already factored most of it in," said Mikio Takada, Nikko Securities general manager.

Tokai Kogyo said its board has decided that the construction firm will apply for court protection under Japanese bankruptcy laws. Under the law, an application for court protection from creditors is widely regarded as a sign that the company is on the verge of failing.
A private credit research firm said Tokai's debts totalled 510 billion yen.

Jitters created by Tokai, which was suspended from trade on both the Tokyo and Osaka bourses in the afternoon, hit some construction shares and also firms said to be on weak financial ground, brokers said.

Shares of supermarket chain operator Yaohan Japan Corp, which announced restructuring plans early in the year, fell 14 yen to 203 in a trade of 6.4 million. It was the second most heavily traded issue on the first section.
Shares of construction firm Aoki Corp fell 11 yen or 8.46 percent to 119, making it the largest percentage loser, while those of Tobishima Corp were down 14 yen at 208.
"It is not as if Tobishima has anything to do with Tokai, but the news sparked selling of similar issues," a broker at a medium-sized brokerage said.
Tokai's major lenders also fell. Shares of Tokai Bank Ltd shed 40 yen to 1,100 and the Long-Term Credit Bank of Japan slipped 22 yen to 438.
"In the short term, the market may be pressured by Tokai, but the sooner ailing firms are cleaned up, the faster the industry will recover," Mitsuru Hayashino, Sanyo Securities general manager, said.
Brokers said however, that the market had been weak even before the Tokai news emerged and trade was lacklustre.
Turnover was 300 million shares, up slightly from the 268 million shares traded on the previous day.
Losers beat winners 801 to 254, while 165 issues were unchanged.
"After the end-June book closings, foreign investors adjusted their portfolios," said Hideo Toriyama, general manager at Tokyo Securities Co Ltd.
Brokers added that pension funds were waiting for a chance to bargain-hunt, but the Nikkei 225 still had a while to go before such moves would emerge.
"Pensions have been buying actively lately and are in no hurry to buy more, especially since the Nikkei average is consolidating," a "Big Four" broker said.
"Investors will start fishing at the bottom when the Nikkei falls into the 19,700-19,900 range," he added.

Brokers added the cautious market mood was also partly due to a lack of evidence that Japan's economy is recovering strongly and due to underlying concerns over the nation's brokerage scandal, which involves top brokers and racketeers.
Gas, pharmaceuticals and oil were the only sectors which posted major gains. Warehouses, rubber, land transport, banks and electric power were at the top of the list of losers.
The TOPIX index shed 11.68 points or 0.76 percent to 1,515.17.

The Nikkei 300 fell 2.47 points or 0.83 percent to 293.55. The second section index was down 10.21 points or 0.56 percent at 1,825.70. Turnover was 9.18 million against 8.6 million on the previous day.
The over-the-counter index was down 5.75 points or 0.47 percent at 1,205.13 in late afternoon Tokyo.
--Masako Iijima, Tokyo Equities Desk (+81-3-3432-9052)
